  2. Layer salad into a wide-mouth mason jar in this order from bottom to top: dressing first, then cherry tomatoes, cucumber, carrots, purple cabbage, romaine on top. This keeps greens from wilting.
  3. Seal and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. When ready to eat, shake vigorously for 10 seconds to distribute dressing, then eat directly from the jar or tip into a bowl.
FODMAP Tip: Purple cabbage is low FODMAP at ¾ cup — this recipe uses ½ cup, keeping it safely within limits. Romaine is fully FODMAP-safe with no quantity restriction. Check your Dijon mustard label; most plain Dijon mustards contain no FODMAPs, but some "honey mustard" varieties add high-FODMAP sweeteners.

Comforting Carrot & Ginger Soup

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 180 cal GF V DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600g (about 6 medium) carrots, peeled and roughly chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 liter (4¼ cups) low-FODMAP vegetable or chicken broth
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 3 tablespoons canned coconut cream (for finishing)

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add fresh ginger and cumin. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.
  2. Add chopped carrots and toss in the oil. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  3. Pour in broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 18–20 minutes until carrots are completely tender when pierced with a fork.
  4. Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend soup until completely smooth — about 60 seconds. Alternatively, transfer in batches to a countertop blender (fill only halfway; hot liquids expand).
  5. Stir in salt and taste. Ladle into bowls and swirl 1 teaspoon coconut cream on top of each serving.
FODMAP Tip: Fresh ginger is low FODMAP and actively supports gut motility — it's one of the few ingredients with research-backed digestive benefits. Ginger powder is also safe. Do not substitute garlic powder for the garlic-infused oil; the fructans in garlic powder are entirely intact and high FODMAP.

Quick Tuna Salad Lettuce Wraps

⏱ 8 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 280 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 cans (140g each) tuna in water, drained
  • 3 tablespoons mayonnaise (check label — no garlic or onion powder)
  • ½ stalk celery, very finely diced
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 6 large butter lettuce or romaine leaves

Instructions

  1. Drain tuna thoroughly, pressing the can lid to extract as much liquid as possible.
  2. In a bowl, combine tuna, mayonnaise, celery, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix with a fork, breaking up any large tuna chunks, until well combined.
  3. Lay lettuce leaves flat on a plate. Spoon about 2–3 tablespoons of tuna mixture into the center of each leaf.
  4. Fold sides of the lettuce inward and eat like a wrap. Serve immediately — these do not hold well once assembled.
FODMAP Tip: Most commercial mayonnaise is FODMAP-safe — Hellmann's Real Mayonnaise contains no FODMAP ingredients. Avoid "flavored" mayo varieties that add garlic or onion. Celery at ½ stalk (roughly 40g per serving across 2 portions) is well within the safe range.

Roasted Red Pepper & Tomato Soup (No Garlic)

⏱ 35 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 160 cal GF V DF

Ingredients

  • 3 large red bell peppers, halved and seeded
  • 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes (no garlic/onion added)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 600ml (2½ cups) low-FODMAP vegetable broth
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1 tablespoon fresh basil, torn (for serving)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven broiler to high. Place red pepper halves skin-side up on a baking sheet. Broil for 10–12 minutes until skins are blackened and blistered all over.
  2. Transfer peppers to a bowl, cover tightly with plastic wrap, and steam for 10 minutes — this makes the skins easy to peel.
  3. Peel and discard the charred skins. Roughly chop the roasted pepper flesh.
  4. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add roasted pepper, crushed tomatoes, broth, and smoked paprika. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
  5. Blend until completely smooth using an immersion blender. Season with salt. Serve in bowls topped with torn basil.
FODMAP Tip: Red bell peppers are low FODMAP and rich in vitamin C. Check crushed tomato labels carefully — many brands add garlic or onion in their "Italian style" varieties. Muir Glen Organic Plain Crushed Tomatoes is a reliable safe option.

Leftover-Stealth Roast Beef Sandwich (Gluten-Free)

⏱ 5 min 👥 1 serving 🔥 440 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 slices gluten-free sandwich bread (Canyon Bakehouse or similar)
  • 90g (3 oz) sliced roast beef (deli or leftover home-roasted)
  • 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
  • 2 tablespoons mayonnaise
  • 2 large romaine lettuce leaves
  • 4 thin slices cucumber
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Toast bread slices lightly if desired — toasting gluten-free bread improves its texture significantly and prevents it from becoming soggy.
  2. Spread Dijon mustard on one slice and mayonnaise on the other.
  3. Layer roast beef, lettuce, and cucumber on the mustard side. Season the beef with black pepper.
  4. Close sandwich. Cut diagonally. If packing for later, wrap tightly in parchment paper and keep the dressing-heavy layers away from the bread — separate the condiment slices slightly before sealing.
FODMAP Tip: When buying deli roast beef, ask if the seasoning contains garlic or onion powder — most do. Either request plain sliced beef or use leftover home-roasted beef where you controlled the seasoning. Canyon Bakehouse GF bread contains no FODMAP triggers and is one of the best-textured GF breads available at standard grocery stores.

Cold Soba Noodle Salad with Peanut Dressing

⏱ 15 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 390 cal V DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 100% buckwheat soba noodles, 100g dry (check label — pure buckwheat, not wheat-blend)
  • 1 cup shredded purple cabbage
  • 1 medium carrot, julienned or grated
  • 3 tablespoons natural peanut butter
  • 2 tablespoons tamari (gluten-free soy sauce)
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, finely grated
  • 2 tablespoons water (to thin dressing)

Instructions

  1. Cook soba noodles according to package directions — typically 4–5 minutes in boiling unsalted water. Drain and rinse under cold running water for 30 seconds to stop cooking and prevent clumping.
  2. Make the dressing: whisk peanut butter, tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil, fresh ginger, and water together until smooth.
  3. In a large bowl, combine cold noodles, shredded cabbage, and julienned carrot.
  4. Pour dressing over the noodle mixture and toss to coat everything evenly. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 24 hours (toss again before serving).
FODMAP Tip: Most soba noodles are made from a blend of buckwheat and wheat flour — this means they are NOT gluten-free. Look specifically for 100% buckwheat soba (Eden Foods makes one). Buckwheat is naturally FODMAP-free. Regular wheat-based soba will cause fructan issues for many IBS sufferers.

Gut-Friendly Greek Salad (No Onion)

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 290 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 medium cucumber, diced into ½-inch pieces
  • 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 60g (about ¼ cup) crumbled feta cheese
  • 12 Kalamata olives, pitted and halved
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar
  • ½ teaspoon dried oregano
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Combine cucumber, cherry tomatoes, feta, and olives in a large bowl.
  2. In a small bowl, whisk garlic-infused oil, red wine vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper until well combined.
  3. Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat without breaking up the feta too much.
  4. Let sit for 5 minutes before serving so flavors meld. Holds well in the fridge for 2 days.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional Greek salad contains raw onion — a major FODMAP trigger. This version simply omits it without losing flavor; the olives, feta, and oregano carry more than enough complexity. Olives are low FODMAP at up to 15 per serving. If using jarred olives, rinse them briefly to reduce sodium.

Creamy Potato & Leek (Green Parts Only) Soup

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 220 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 3 medium Russet potatoes (about 600g), peeled and diced into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 leeks — green tops only, washed and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 liter (4¼ cups) low-FODMAP chicken or vegetable broth
  • ¼ cup lactose-free cream or coconut cream
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon white pepper

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add leek greens and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
  2. Add potato cubes and broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15–18 minutes until potatoes are completely tender when pierced.
  3. Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend until smooth and creamy. Alternatively, mash with a potato masher for a chunkier texture.
  4. Stir in lactose-free cream, salt, and white pepper. Reheat gently over low heat for 2 minutes if needed. Ladle into bowls.
FODMAP Tip: This is the most critical leek rule: the white and light green base of the leek is HIGH in fructans — never use it. The dark green tops are low FODMAP at ½ cup per serving. Slice off and discard the white bulb entirely before cooking. This one swap makes all the difference.

The 10-Minute Egg Salad

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 270 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 large eggs
  • 3 tablespoons mayonnaise
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • ½ stalk celery, very finely diced
  • 2 tablespoons fresh chives, finely chopped
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika (for finishing)

Instructions

  1. Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook for exactly 10 minutes for fully hard-boiled yolks.
  2. Transfer eggs to an ice bath (cold water + ice cubes) and let sit for 5 minutes. Peel under running water.
  3. Chop eggs into roughly ¼-inch pieces. Transfer to a bowl.
  4. Add mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, celery, and chives. Fold gently to combine — do not overmix or the yolks will become gluey. Season with salt.
  5. Serve on GF toast or in lettuce cups. Dust with smoked paprika before serving.
FODMAP Tip: Eggs have absolutely no FODMAP content. They're one of the most gut-neutral proteins available. If you have pre-boiled eggs in the fridge, this recipe takes literally 3 minutes. Make a batch of 6 eggs on Sunday and you'll have the base for multiple lunches.

Zesty Quinoa Tabbouleh (Parsley & Mint Base)

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 200 cal GF V DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 cup white quinoa, rinsed and cooked (yields about 3 cups cooked)
  • 1½ cups fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped (about 1 large bunch)
  • ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
  • 1 cup cherry tomatoes, quartered
  • 1 medium cucumber, diced into ¼-inch pieces
  • 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt

Instructions

  1. Cook quinoa and let cool to room temperature — warm quinoa will wilt the herbs.
  2. Combine cooled quinoa, parsley, mint, tomatoes, and cucumber in a large bowl.
  3. Whisk lemon juice, garlic-infused oil, and salt in a small bowl. Pour over the salad.
  4. Toss thoroughly. Taste and adjust lemon juice or salt as needed. Let sit for 10 minutes before serving for flavors to develop. Stores in the fridge for 3 days.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional tabbouleh uses bulgur wheat — high in fructans. Quinoa is a perfect low-FODMAP swap that also adds protein. Fresh parsley is FODMAP-free and can be used generously. The lemon juice also acts as a mild digestive support.

Anti-Inflammatory Turmeric Chicken Soup

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 290 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 medium chicken breasts (about 400g)
  • 1 liter (4¼ cups) low-FODMAP chicken broth
  • 2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced
  • 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
  • ½ teaspoon ground ginger
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper (activates turmeric's curcumin)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped (for serving)

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add turmeric, ginger, and black pepper. Stir for 30 seconds — the fat in the oil helps release the fat-soluble compounds in turmeric.
  2. Add whole chicken breasts. Pour in broth. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
  3. Add carrots. Cook at a gentle simmer (not a boil) for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
  4. Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return to the pot. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt if needed.
  5. Ladle into bowls and top with fresh cilantro.
FODMAP Tip: Turmeric contains curcumin, which has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties in gut tissue in multiple studies. Black pepper increases curcumin absorption by up to 2,000% — this is not folklore, it's pharmacokinetics. Add the pepper. Both spices are fully FODMAP-safe.

Hearty Kale & Walnut Salad with Feta

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 340 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 cups curly kale, ribs removed and leaves roughly torn
  • ¼ cup walnut halves, roughly chopped
  • 40g (3 tablespoons) crumbled feta cheese
  • ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt

Instructions

  1. Place torn kale in a large bowl. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of the garlic-infused oil directly onto the kale. Using your hands, massage the kale for 2 minutes until the leaves soften, darken in color, and reduce in volume by about half. This step is essential — raw kale is tough; massaged kale is tender.
  2. Whisk remaining oil with lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and salt to make the dressing.
  3. Add cherry tomatoes, walnuts, and feta to the massaged kale. Pour dressing over and toss to combine.
  4. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 2 days — massaged kale holds its texture much better than romaine.
FODMAP Tip: Kale is low FODMAP — but at a cautious serving size of about ½ cup cooked or 1 cup raw. This recipe uses 4 cups raw for 2 servings, which becomes approximately 1 cup raw per person after massaging. Walnuts are low FODMAP at 10 halves (30g) per serving — this recipe uses less.

Spinach & Strawberry Salad with Balsamic Glaze

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 240 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 cups fresh baby spinach
  • 1 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
  • 30g (about 2 tablespoons) crumbled feta cheese
  • 2 tablespoons sliced almonds
  • 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon maple syrup
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt

Instructions

  1. Make balsamic glaze: combine balsamic vinegar and maple syrup in a small saucepan over medium heat. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half and syrupy. Remove from heat and let cool 2 minutes — it will thicken further as it cools.
  2. In a large salad bowl, toss spinach with garlic-infused oil and salt until lightly coated.
  3. Add strawberries, feta, and sliced almonds. Toss gently.
  4. Drizzle the balsamic glaze over the top from a height to create a decorative drizzle pattern. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Balsamic vinegar is low FODMAP at 1 tablespoon per serving — this recipe uses 1 tablespoon per serving across 2 portions. Larger amounts of balsamic can become a trigger due to concentrated fructose. Sliced almonds are safe at 12 whole almonds (about 2 tablespoons sliced) per serving.

Savory Butternut Squash Soup

⏱ 35 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 200 cal GF V DF

Ingredients

  • 1 small butternut squash (about 700g), peeled, seeded, and cubed
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 800ml (3½ cups) low-FODMAP vegetable broth
  • ½ teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 2 tablespoons hulled pumpkin seeds (pepitas), toasted, for topping

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add squash cubes and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until edges begin to caramelize lightly.
  2. Add broth, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes until squash is completely soft when pressed with a spoon.
  3. Blend until smooth using an immersion blender. Season with salt. If soup is too thick, add water in ¼ cup increments until desired consistency is reached.
  4. Ladle into bowls. Top each serving with ½ tablespoon of toasted pumpkin seeds for texture and protein. Stores refrigerated for 5 days.
FODMAP Tip: Butternut squash is low FODMAP at ¼ cup (about 45g) per serving — this recipe divides roughly 700g across 4 servings (approximately 175g per serving), which may exceed the safe threshold. To stay safe, reduce squash to 500g total, or serve smaller portions paired with a side protein.

The "No-Chop" Cucumber & Radish Salad

⏱ 5 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 120 cal GF V DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 large English cucumber, sliced into thin rounds using a mandoline or peeler
  • 6 radishes, thinly sliced
  • 2 tablespoons rice vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1 teaspoon maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon fresh dill, roughly torn
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1 teaspoon sesame seeds (for topping)

Instructions

  1. Arrange cucumber and radish slices in a single overlapping layer in a shallow bowl.
  2. Whisk rice vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup, and salt in a small bowl. Pour over the vegetables.
  3. Scatter dill and sesame seeds on top. Let sit for 3 minutes before serving so the vegetables absorb the dressing slightly. Serve cold.
FODMAP Tip: Radishes are low FODMAP and have a pleasant peppery bite that adds complexity without triggering symptoms. Cucumber has essentially no FODMAP load. This salad works well as a side dish alongside any protein in this book.

Light Miso Soup with Tofu Cubes

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 130 cal GF V DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600ml (2½ cups) hot water (not boiling — 170°F / 75°C)
  • 2 tablespoons white miso paste (shiro miso)
  • 100g firm tofu, drained and cut into ½-inch cubes
  • 1 tablespoon dried wakame seaweed, rehydrated in water for 5 minutes
  • 2 spring onions — green tops only, thinly sliced
  • 1 teaspoon tamari (GF soy sauce) — optional for extra depth

Instructions

  1. Heat water to approximately 170°F (75°C) — you want it hot but not boiling. Boiling water destroys the beneficial probiotics in miso.
  2. Place miso paste in a small bowl. Add 3 tablespoons of the hot water and whisk until paste is fully dissolved with no lumps.
  3. Divide dissolved miso between two bowls. Pour remaining hot water over it.
  4. Add tofu cubes, drained wakame, and spring onion greens to each bowl. Add a few drops of tamari if desired. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: White miso (shiro miso) is low FODMAP at 2 tablespoons per serving. Firm tofu is low FODMAP — the processing removes most of the isoflavones that affect gut sensitivity. Use only the dark green tops of spring onions; the white bulb contains significant fructans. Never use a full onion here.

Portable Turkey Meatball Bento Box

⏱ 25 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 460 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 250g lean ground turkey
  • ¼ cup gluten-free breadcrumbs
  • 1 large egg
  • ½ teaspoon dried oregano
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 cup cooked white rice (for the bento)
  • 1 cup sliced cucumber and carrots (for the bento)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Combine ground turkey, GF breadcrumbs, egg, oregano, and salt in a bowl. Mix with hands until just combined.
  3. Roll into 12 equal meatballs (about 20g each). Place on prepared baking sheet. Drizzle with garlic-infused oil.
  4. Bake for 16–18 minutes until meatballs are golden and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
  5. Pack bento boxes with 6 meatballs per person, ½ cup rice, and ½ cup raw vegetables. Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
FODMAP Tip: These meatballs are genuinely desk-friendly — they're not pungent and reheat well. Check GF breadcrumb labels: some add onion or garlic powder. Ian's Gluten-Free Panko Breadcrumbs are consistently clean. Alternatively, crush plain GF rice crackers as a breadcrumb substitute.

Creamy (Lactose-Free) Tomato Basil Soup

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 190 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 cans (400g each) crushed tomatoes (no garlic/onion added)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 600ml (2½ cups) low-FODMAP vegetable broth
  • ¼ cup lactose-free heavy cream or full-fat coconut cream
  • 1 teaspoon cane sugar
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn (divided between serving and finishing)

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute.
  2. Add crushed tomatoes, broth, sugar, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sugar reduces the natural acidity of canned tomatoes.
  3. Blend until smooth. Return to pot over low heat.
  4. Stir in lactose-free cream and half the basil. Heat for 2 minutes. Do not boil after adding cream.
  5. Ladle into bowls and top with remaining torn basil leaves.
FODMAP Tip: Canned tomatoes can vary significantly in FODMAP content based on concentration. Plain crushed tomatoes at ½ cup per serving are generally safe; avoid "tomato paste" as a base, which is highly concentrated and can trigger fructose issues. The small amount of sugar (¼ teaspoon per serving) is well within safe limits.

Chapter 7: 30-Minute Family Dinners

The first time Anya made the Spaghetti Bolognese from this chapter, her ten-year-old ate two full bowls and asked for it again the next day. She texted me at 8 PM: "He doesn't know it's FODMAP and I don't care." That's the whole point of this chapter.

Fakeout Takeout & One-Pan Wonders

The "30-minute" claim in cookbooks is one of the most abused lies in publishing. I know because I've tested them all, standing at my stove with a timer, waiting for the author's optimistic estimate to fall apart at the sixteen-minute mark. Every recipe in this chapter has been clocked, including the washing-up. When I say 30 minutes, I mean 30 minutes from the moment you open the fridge.

The strategy here is the "family stealth" model. These dinners look, smell, and taste like the takeout or comfort food your family already loves. The Pad Thai doesn't taste low FODMAP. The Bolognese doesn't taste like it's missing anything. The Mac and Cheese gets eaten by children who haven't touched a vegetable since October. The substitutions are invisible — garlic-infused oil instead of garlic cloves, green spring onion tops instead of onion, gluten-free pasta cooked in well-salted water so it doesn't taste like cardboard.

A few techniques that make everything in this chapter work. First, always salt your pasta water aggressively — 1 full teaspoon of sea salt per quart of water. GF pasta has a bland baseline; unsalted water guarantees something that tastes like wet paper. Second, use a hot pan. Stir-fries and sautés need high heat to develop flavor through the Maillard reaction — low heat just steams everything gray. Third, rest your proteins. A chicken breast that's been rested for three minutes after cooking loses 30% less juice when you cut it. These aren't advanced techniques; they're just the ones most cookbooks skip because they're not glamorous.

These 25 dinners cost under $10 per meal using ingredients from a standard US grocery store. That's not a claim — it's a budget I built these recipes around, shopping at Kroger with a calculator.

The "Stealth" Spaghetti Bolognese (Garlic-Infused Oil)

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 510 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 300g gluten-free spaghetti
  • 400g lean ground beef
  • 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes (no garlic/onion)
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 medium carrot, finely grated
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • ½ teaspoon dried basil
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 4 fresh basil leaves (for serving)

Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of well-salted water (1 tsp salt per quart) to a boil. Cook GF spaghetti 1 minute less than package directions — it will finish cooking in the sauce.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it into fine crumbles, until deeply browned with no pink remaining.
  3. Add grated carrot, oregano, and dried basil. Cook for 2 minutes until carrot softens.
  4. Add crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Reduce heat and simmer for 8 minutes.
  5. Drain pasta, reserving ¼ cup pasta water. Add pasta directly to the sauce. Toss over medium heat for 1 minute, adding pasta water if needed to loosen. Serve topped with fresh basil.
FODMAP Tip: Grated carrot is the "stealth" vegetable here — it disappears into the sauce but adds natural sweetness and body. This replaces the standard soffritto (onion, celery, carrot) by dropping onion entirely. Nobody in your family will notice.

One-Pan Lemon-Herb Roast Chicken & Potatoes

⏱ 45 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 480 cal GF DF

Ingredients

  • 4 bone-in chicken thighs (about 800g), skin-on
  • 4 medium Yukon Gold potatoes (about 600g), quartered
  • 3 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 lemon — zest and juice
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
  • 1 teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). In a large bowl, whisk garlic-infused oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper to make the marinade.
  2. Add potatoes to the marinade. Toss to coat thoroughly. Transfer to a large baking sheet and spread in a single layer.
  3. Add chicken thighs to the same bowl with remaining marinade. Toss to coat. Place skin-side up directly on top of or beside the potatoes on the baking sheet.
  4. Roast at 425°F for 35–40 minutes until chicken skin is deeply golden and crispy and potatoes are tender with caramelized edges. Chicken internal temperature should reach 165°F (74°C).
  5. Let rest 3 minutes before serving. Spoon pan juices over everything.
FODMAP Tip: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs stay juicy at high oven temperatures and are significantly more forgiving than chicken breasts. The pan drippings from skin-on thighs add natural flavor that doesn't require garlic or onion to taste complete.

20-Minute Beef Stir-Fry with Bok Choy

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 380 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 450g (1 lb) beef sirloin, thinly sliced against the grain
  • 4 heads baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
  • 2 tablespoons tamari (GF soy sauce)
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, finely grated
  • 1 tablespoon cornstarch
  • 2 cups cooked white rice (for serving)

Instructions

  1. Toss sliced beef with cornstarch and 1 tablespoon tamari. Set aside for 5 minutes — the cornstarch velvets the meat and creates a glossy sauce.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large wok or skillet over very high heat until just smoking — this is the most important step for stir-fry flavor.
  3. Add beef in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 90 seconds to develop a brown crust, then toss for 60 seconds more. Remove beef from pan and set aside.
  4. Add bok choy cut-side down to the same hot pan. Cook for 2 minutes without moving, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
  5. Return beef to pan. Add remaining tablespoon tamari, sesame oil, and fresh ginger. Toss everything together over high heat for 60 seconds. Serve immediately over white rice.
FODMAP Tip: Bok choy is fully low FODMAP and one of the best stir-fry vegetables for this diet. Slice beef against the grain — this shortens the muscle fibers and makes even budget cuts of sirloin tender after a quick high-heat cook.

Gluten-Free Mac & Cheese (Family Approved)

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 540 cal GF VG 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 300g gluten-free elbow pasta (rice-based recommended)
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 2 tablespoons gluten-free all-purpose flour
  • 1½ cups lactose-free whole milk, warmed
  • 1½ cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly grated (not pre-shredded)
  • ½ teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon white pepper

Instructions

  1. Cook GF pasta in well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than package directions. Drain and set aside.
  2. Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add GF flour and whisk constantly for 90 seconds to cook out the raw flour taste — the mixture should turn golden and smell nutty.
  3. Slowly pour in warm lactose-free milk, whisking continuously to prevent lumps. Cook for 3–4 minutes until sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
  4. Remove from heat. Add grated cheddar in three batches, stirring after each addition until fully melted. Stir in Dijon mustard, salt, and white pepper.
  5. Add cooked pasta to the cheese sauce. Toss over medium-low heat for 1 minute until every piece is coated. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Pre-shredded cheese contains anti-caking agents (often made from potato starch or cellulose) that prevent the cheese from melting properly and create a grainy sauce. Always grate your own. Cheddar is naturally low in lactose due to the aging process — hard aged cheeses are among the safest dairy products on the protocol.

Sheet Pan Maple-Mustard Salmon & Green Beans

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 430 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 salmon fillets (about 150g each), skin-on
  • 400g fresh green beans, trimmed
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 lemon, sliced into thin rounds

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Whisk maple syrup, Dijon mustard, garlic-infused oil, salt, and pepper to make the glaze.
  3. Arrange green beans on one side of the baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the glaze and toss to coat. Spread in a single layer.
  4. Place salmon fillets skin-side down on the other side. Spoon remaining glaze over the salmon. Place lemon rounds on top of fillets.
  5. Roast for 12–15 minutes until salmon flakes easily when pressed with a fork and green beans have charred slightly at the tips. Serve directly from the pan.
FODMAP Tip: Green beans are low FODMAP at ½ cup (about 75g) per serving — this recipe distributes 400g across 4 servings (100g each), which is slightly above the most conservative estimates. If you are highly sensitive, reduce green beans to 300g total or substitute with zucchini rounds, which have no FODMAP concerns.

The Easy Chicken Pad Thai (No Onion)

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 490 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 200g flat rice noodles (8mm width)
  • 2 chicken breasts (about 400g), thinly sliced
  • 2 large eggs
  • 3 tablespoons tamari (GF soy sauce)
  • 2 tablespoons natural peanut butter
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon brown sugar
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused peanut oil or vegetable oil
  • ¼ cup green spring onion tops, thinly sliced
  • ¼ cup roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
  • 1 lime, cut into wedges

Instructions

  1. Soak rice noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable but not fully soft. Drain and set aside.
  2. Make sauce: whisk tamari, peanut butter, rice vinegar, and brown sugar until smooth.
  3. Heat oil in a large wok over very high heat. Add chicken slices and cook for 3–4 minutes, tossing, until golden and cooked through. Push to the side.
  4. Crack eggs into the cleared space and scramble for 1 minute until just set. Mix with chicken.
  5. Add drained noodles and pour sauce over everything. Toss constantly over high heat for 2–3 minutes until noodles are fully cooked and coated. Serve topped with spring onion greens, peanuts, and lime wedges.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional Pad Thai uses shallots — high FODMAP. This version replaces them with spring onion greens, which add the same fresh allium note without the fructan load. The peanut butter in the sauce also boosts protein significantly, making this a genuinely complete meal.

Gentle Turkey Chili (No Beans, High Flavor)

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 350 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 500g lean ground turkey
  • 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes (no garlic/onion)
  • 1 large red bell pepper, diced
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 teaspoons ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon chili powder (check label — pure chili powder, no onion)
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ cup green spring onion tops, sliced (for topping)

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add ground turkey. Cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking into crumbles, until browned all over.
  2. Add diced red pepper. Cook for 3 minutes until pepper softens slightly.
  3. Add cumin, smoked paprika, and chili powder. Stir for 60 seconds to toast the spices in the fat — this step dramatically deepens the flavor.
  4. Add diced tomatoes with their juices. Stir well and bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chili thickens. Season with salt.
  5. Serve in bowls topped with spring onion greens. Pairs well with plain white rice or corn tortilla chips.
FODMAP Tip: Kidney beans and black beans — the standard chili base — are high FODMAP and off the table during elimination. This recipe replaces them with extra turkey and bell pepper for body, and toasting the spice blend creates a depth of flavor that most bean-based chilis can't match. If you're past the reintroduction phase and tolerate canned, rinsed kidney beans, ½ cup per serving is your conservative limit.

Crispy Baked Chicken Tenders (GF)

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 380 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600g chicken breast tenders (or breasts cut into 1-inch strips)
  • 1 cup gluten-free panko breadcrumbs (Ian's GF Panko)
  • ¼ cup gluten-free all-purpose flour
  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Place a wire rack on a baking sheet and spray lightly with oil — this allows air to circulate and prevents soggy bottoms.
  2. Set up three shallow bowls: flour with salt and pepper in the first, beaten eggs in the second, panko mixed with smoked paprika in the third.
  3. Coat each chicken strip in flour (shake off excess), dip in egg, then press firmly into panko so all sides are coated. Place on the wire rack.
  4. Drizzle garlic-infused oil evenly over the coated strips.
  5. Bake at 425°F for 16–18 minutes until panko is deep golden and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Serve immediately with Dijon mustard as a dipping sauce.
FODMAP Tip: GF panko is essential for the crunch here — regular GF breadcrumbs become dense when baked. The wire rack is non-negotiable for crispiness; a flat baking sheet results in steamed, soft bottoms. Kids love these as much as anything from a fast-food menu — that's the whole point.

Pork Chops with Sage & Polenta

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 500 cal GF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 bone-in pork chops (about 200g each), 1 inch thick
  • 1 cup polenta (not instant)
  • 3 cups low-FODMAP chicken broth (for polenta)
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 6 fresh sage leaves
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt (for chops)
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Bring broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly pour in polenta while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring every 2 minutes, for 20–22 minutes until polenta is thick and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
  2. While polenta cooks, pat pork chops completely dry with paper towels — this is essential for a good sear. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
  3. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add pork chops. Cook undisturbed for 4–5 minutes per side until a deep mahogany crust develops. Internal temperature should reach 145°F (63°C).
  4. Remove pork chops and let rest for 3 minutes. Add butter and sage leaves to the same hot pan. Cook for 1–2 minutes until sage is crispy and butter is golden brown.
  5. Stir 1 tablespoon butter into polenta. Divide polenta among plates. Top with a pork chop. Spoon sage-brown butter over each serving.
FODMAP Tip: Polenta (ground cornmeal) is naturally gluten-free and FODMAP-free — a versatile base that works as a swap for mashed potatoes, pasta, or rice. Sage is fully FODMAP-safe and supports digestive comfort. The key to restaurant-quality pork chops is a completely dry surface before searing — moisture prevents browning.

"Better-Than-Takeout" Pineapple Fried Rice

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 440 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 3 cups cooked white rice (day-old rice works best)
  • 200g shrimp or diced chicken breast, cooked
  • ½ cup fresh pineapple, cut into small cubes (not canned in syrup)
  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 1 cup frozen peas (remove — see tip)
  • 3 tablespoons tamari (GF soy sauce)
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused vegetable oil
  • ¼ cup green spring onion tops, sliced

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large wok over very high heat until nearly smoking. Add cold rice and spread in a thin layer — let it sit undisturbed for 2 minutes to develop a slight crust.
  2. Push rice to the side. Pour beaten eggs into the cleared space. Scramble for 60 seconds until just set, then fold into the rice.
  3. Add cooked protein and pineapple cubes. Toss continuously for 2 minutes.
  4. Pour tamari and sesame oil around the edges of the wok (not directly into the center) — this briefly hits the hot metal and creates a caramelized base note. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
  5. Serve topped with spring onion greens.
FODMAP Tip: Peas are low FODMAP at ¼ cup per serving — if you add the full 1 cup across 4 servings (¼ cup each), it stays within safe limits. Fresh pineapple is low FODMAP at ¾ cup per serving; canned pineapple in syrup adds concentrated fructose and should be avoided. Day-old cold rice fries better than freshly cooked rice because the grains are drier and separate more easily.

Soothing Coconut Chicken Curry

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 490 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600g chicken breast, cut into 1½-inch chunks
  • 1 can (400ml) full-fat coconut milk
  • 1 can (200g) diced tomatoes (no garlic/onion)
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 teaspoons curry powder (check label — no onion powder)
  • 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
  • ½ teaspoon ground ginger
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks and cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until golden on the outside (they don't need to be fully cooked yet).
  2. Add curry powder, turmeric, and ginger. Stir for 60 seconds to coat the chicken and bloom the spices in the oil.
  3. Pour in coconut milk and diced tomatoes. Stir well. Bring to a simmer and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is fully cooked and sauce has thickened slightly. Season with salt.
  4. Serve over white rice with cilantro scattered on top.
FODMAP Tip: Check curry powder blends carefully — many commercial blends include onion powder or garlic powder as fillers. Spice Islands Curry Powder and McCormick Curry Powder are generally clean; verify each batch. Making your own blend from individual safe spices (turmeric, cumin, coriander, ginger, paprika) ensures zero surprises.

Zucchini Noodle "Zoodles" with Homemade Pesto

⏱ 15 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 340 cal GF VG DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 3 medium zucchini (about 500g), spiralized or peeled into ribbons
  • 1½ cups fresh basil leaves, packed
  • 3 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons pine nuts
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 30g (2 tablespoons) freshly grated Parmesan
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt

Instructions

  1. Make pesto: blend basil, garlic-infused oil, pine nuts, lemon juice, Parmesan, and salt in a food processor or blender until smooth, about 45 seconds. Taste and adjust lemon or salt.
  2. If using a spiralizer, process zucchini now. Pat zoodles dry with paper towels to reduce moisture.
  3. Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add zoodles and cook, tossing, for 2–3 minutes until just tender — they should have a slight bite and not be mushy. This is the critical timing window.
  4. Remove from heat immediately. Add pesto and toss to coat. Plate and serve within 2 minutes before the zucchini releases more water.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional pesto uses garlic cloves — swap directly with garlic-infused oil. The flavor is indistinguishable once combined with basil and Parmesan. Pine nuts are low FODMAP at 1 tablespoon per serving. Do not overcook the zoodles — they release significant water if heated too long, diluting the pesto.

Quick Shrimp Tacos on Corn Tortillas

⏱ 15 min 👥 4 servings (8 tacos) 🔥 380 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 400g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 8 small corn tortillas (100% corn, no wheat blend)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1 cup shredded purple cabbage
  • ½ cup fresh tomato, diced
  • 2 limes, cut into wedges
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions

  1. Toss shrimp with garlic-infused oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and salt.
  2. Heat a large skillet over high heat for 1 minute. Add shrimp in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 90 seconds until pink and curled at the bottom, then flip and cook for 60 seconds more until just cooked through. Do not overcook — overcooked shrimp are rubbery.
  3. Warm corn tortillas directly over a gas burner for 20 seconds per side (or in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side) until lightly charred and flexible.
  4. Assemble tacos: shrimp first, then cabbage and tomato. Finish with a squeeze of lime juice and fresh cilantro.
FODMAP Tip: Always check corn tortilla ingredients — some brands blend in wheat flour. Look for "100% stone-ground corn" or check the ingredients for wheat. Mission Gluten Free Tortillas are widely available and clean. Corn tortillas are naturally gluten-free and FODMAP-safe.

The Perfect "Safe" Hamburger (GF Bun)

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 560 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600g 80/20 ground beef
  • 4 gluten-free hamburger buns (Canyon Bakehouse or Schar)
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 4 slices aged cheddar cheese
  • 4 large romaine lettuce leaves
  • 1 large tomato, sliced into 8 rounds
  • 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard and 2 tablespoons mayonnaise

Instructions

  1. Divide ground beef into 4 equal portions (150g each). Shape into patties slightly wider than your buns — they will shrink about 20% during cooking. Press a ½-inch thumbprint into the center of each patty to prevent doming.
  2. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper immediately before cooking — not before, as salt draws out moisture.
  3. Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add patties — do not press down. Cook for 3–4 minutes per side for medium (internal temp 160°F / 71°C). Place cheese on patties during the last 60 seconds of cooking.
  4. Toast bun cut-sides in the same skillet for 30 seconds. Assemble: condiments on bun, then lettuce, tomato, patty. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: 80/20 ground beef needs no added binders or seasonings — don't add breadcrumbs or Worcestershire sauce (most contain garlic/onion). The fat content is what makes burgers flavorful. Aged cheddar is low in lactose. Standard ketchup typically contains high-fructose corn syrup — Dijon mustard and mayo are better condiment choices for this protocol.

Baked Cod with Lemon & Parsley Butter

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 290 cal GF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 cod fillets (about 150g each)
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened
  • 3 tablespoons fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
  • 1 lemon — zest and 1 tablespoon juice
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking dish with parchment paper.
  2. Make parsley butter: mash together softened butter, chopped parsley, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper with a fork until well combined.
  3. Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels and place in the baking dish. Season tops with smoked paprika. Place a generous tablespoon of parsley butter on top of each fillet.
  4. Bake for 12–15 minutes until cod is opaque, flakes easily with a fork, and no translucent center remains. Do not overbake — cod goes from perfect to dry quickly after 15 minutes.
  5. Serve immediately with pan juices spooned over each fillet.
FODMAP Tip: Fish has zero FODMAP content — it's one of the safest proteins on the protocol. The butter here contributes negligible lactose (butter is mostly fat). The parsley butter can be made in advance and stored in the fridge for up to 5 days, or rolled in parchment and frozen for 3 months.

Sausage (No Garlic) & Red Pepper Skillet

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 410 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 Italian-style pork sausages (check label — no garlic or onion listed)
  • 3 large red bell peppers, sliced into ½-inch strips
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon dried fennel seeds
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 2 tablespoons fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped

Instructions

  1. Slice sausages diagonally into ½-inch rounds.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage rounds and cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until golden brown on both sides.
  3. Add bell pepper strips, fennel seeds, and smoked paprika. Toss to combine. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until peppers are softened with slightly caramelized edges and sausage is fully cooked through.
  4. Season with salt. Scatter fresh parsley over the top. Serve with white rice, polenta, or GF crusty bread for mopping up the pan juices.
FODMAP Tip: Finding sausages without garlic or onion is genuinely hard — most mass-market Italian sausages include both. Aidells Chicken & Apple Sausages are one commercially available option without alliums. Alternatively, make your own patties using the turkey breakfast patty recipe in Chapter 5, shaped into rounds here.

Low-Stress Chicken Piccata

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 390 cal GF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 chicken breasts (about 150g each), butterflied or pounded to ½-inch thickness
  • ¼ cup gluten-free all-purpose flour (for dredging)
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter (divided)
  • ½ cup low-FODMAP chicken broth
  • 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons capers, rinsed
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped

Instructions

  1. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Dredge both sides lightly in GF flour, shaking off excess.
  2. Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until foaming. Add chicken and cook 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through (165°F / 74°C). Transfer to a plate.
  3. Add broth to the same hot pan, scraping up any browned bits with a wooden spoon — this deglazing step builds the sauce's flavor base. Cook for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
  4. Add lemon juice and capers. Swirl in remaining 1 tablespoon cold butter — this emulsifies the sauce and gives it a glossy, restaurant-quality finish.
  5. Return chicken to the pan for 60 seconds to coat in the sauce. Serve immediately, spooning sauce generously over each portion. Top with fresh parsley.
FODMAP Tip: Capers are FODMAP-free and add the signature briny punch that defines piccata. Rinse them from their brine before use to control the salt level. The GF flour in the dredge provides almost no FODMAP load at these quantities — it's primarily a surface-coating technique, not a thickener.

Beef & Broccoli Teriyaki Bowl

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 460 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 450g beef sirloin, thinly sliced
  • 3 cups broccoli florets (about 300g)
  • 3 tablespoons tamari
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon cornstarch
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 cups cooked white rice

Instructions

  1. Make teriyaki sauce: whisk tamari, maple syrup, rice vinegar, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Set aside.
  2. Toss sliced beef with cornstarch until evenly coated.
  3. Steam broccoli florets for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender. Drain.
  4. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large wok over very high heat. Add beef in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 90 seconds until browned, then toss for 60 seconds. Push beef to the side.
  5. Add broccoli to the pan. Pour teriyaki sauce over everything. Toss and cook for 2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats the beef and broccoli in a glossy glaze. Serve over white rice.
FODMAP Tip: Broccoli is low FODMAP at ¾ cup (about 75g) per serving — this recipe uses 300g across 4 servings (75g each), right at the safe threshold. Do not use the broccoli stalk or stems here — they are higher in fructans than the florets. The cornstarch creates the characteristic glossy restaurant-style sauce without any FODMAP ingredients.

Rustic Shepherd's Pie (FODMAP-Friendly)

⏱ 50 min 👥 6 servings 🔥 440 cal GF

Ingredients

  • 600g lean ground lamb or beef
  • 1 kg (about 6 medium) Russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
  • 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 cup low-FODMAP beef or chicken broth
  • 1 tablespoon tomato paste (plain, no added garlic/onion)
  • 3 tablespoons lactose-free butter and ¼ cup lactose-free milk (for mash)
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Boil potato cubes in salted water for 15–18 minutes until fork-tender. Drain. Mash with lactose-free butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt.
  2. While potatoes cook, heat garlic-infused oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground meat and cook for 6–7 minutes until browned.
  3. Add carrots, tomato paste, and broth. Stir well. Simmer for 10 minutes until carrots soften and liquid reduces by half.
  4. Preheat oven broiler to high. Spoon mashed potato over the meat filling and smooth with a spatula into an even layer. Use a fork to create ridges on the surface — these will brown and crisp under the broiler.
  5. Broil for 4–5 minutes until mashed potato top is golden brown and bubbling at the edges. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional shepherd's pie uses onion and garlic as the flavor base — both replaced here. The garlic-infused oil plus tomato paste provides surprisingly deep savory flavor. This recipe is excellent for family dinners: make it Sunday, portion and refrigerate, and reheat single servings all week.

Crispy Skin Trout with Roasted Carrots

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 390 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 rainbow trout fillets (about 150g each), skin-on
  • 500g carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch sticks
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil (divided)
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt (divided)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh dill, chopped
  • 1 lemon, cut into wedges

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss carrot sticks with 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil, thyme, and ¼ teaspoon salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20–22 minutes until tender with caramelized edges.
  2. When carrots have 8 minutes left, start the trout. Pat fillets completely dry — any moisture will prevent crispy skin. Season skin side only with smoked paprika and remaining salt.
  3. Heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a nonstick skillet over high heat until shimmering. Lay trout skin-side down. Press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds to ensure full contact with the pan. Cook for 4 minutes undisturbed until skin is deeply golden and the flesh is opaque 80% of the way up.
  4. Flip and cook 1 minute more. Serve immediately over roasted carrots. Top with fresh dill and lemon wedges.
FODMAP Tip: The trick to crispy fish skin is high heat, dry skin, and patience. The skin must not be moved for those 4 minutes. Trout cooks faster than salmon — watch it carefully to avoid overcooking the delicate flesh.

Ground Turkey "Sloppy Joes"

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 460 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 500g lean ground turkey
  • 1 can (200g) tomato sauce (no garlic/onion)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 4 GF hamburger buns, toasted

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground turkey and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking into fine crumbles, until fully browned.
  2. Drain any excess fat from the pan by tilting it and spooning off the liquid.
  3. Add tomato sauce, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, Dijon mustard, and salt. Stir to combine.
  4. Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens to a saucy consistency that holds its shape briefly when stirred. Taste and adjust sweetness or acid.
  5. Spoon generously onto toasted GF buns. Serve immediately with napkins nearby.
FODMAP Tip: Standard Sloppy Joe seasoning packets contain onion and garlic powder — skip them entirely. This sauce uses the same balance of sweet, tangy, and savory achieved through maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, and Dijon. It's genuinely better than the packet version.

Chicken Skewers with Peanut Satay Sauce

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 420 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
  • ¼ cup natural peanut butter
  • 3 tablespoons tamari
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, finely grated
  • 3 tablespoons water (to thin sauce)
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
  • 8 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 15 minutes

Instructions

  1. Make satay sauce: whisk peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, fresh ginger, and water until smooth and pourable. Reserve half for serving.
  2. Toss chicken cubes with garlic-infused oil and 2 tablespoons of the satay sauce. Thread onto pre-soaked skewers — about 5–6 pieces per skewer.
  3. Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Cook skewers for 4–5 minutes per side, turning once, until chicken is golden with slight char marks and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
  4. Serve immediately with remaining satay sauce on the side for dipping.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional satay often includes shallots or garlic — this version omits both entirely. The ginger, tamari, and peanut butter create the same complex, savory-sweet profile. Soaking wooden skewers prevents them from burning during grilling — 15 minutes minimum.

Lemon-Dill Baked Salmon

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 360 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 salmon fillets (about 150g each), skin-on
  • 2 tablespoons fresh dill, finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 4 thin lemon rounds (for topping)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking dish with parchment paper.
  2. Whisk garlic-infused oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
  3. Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the baking dish. Brush liberally with the lemon-oil mixture. Scatter fresh dill over each fillet and lay a lemon round on top.
  4. Bake for 12–14 minutes until salmon is opaque and flakes easily when pressed with a fork in the thickest part. The flesh should be just barely set in the center — this is perfect medium doneness. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.
FODMAP Tip: Salmon is one of the most nutrient-dense proteins for IBS management — high in omega-3 fatty acids, which have demonstrated anti-inflammatory effects on gut tissue in research studies. Fresh dill is fully FODMAP-safe and pairs naturally with fish. This recipe works equally well with trout, cod, or halibut fillets.

Easy Chicken Cacciatore (Tomato & Herb Base)

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 430 cal GF DF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 180g each)
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil, divided
  • 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes, no added onion or garlic
  • 1 cup red bell pepper, sliced into thin strips
  • ½ cup pitted black olives
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped (to serve)

Instructions

  1. Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
  2. Heat 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down and sear for 5–6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and releases naturally from the pan. Flip and sear the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
  3. Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the same pan. Add red bell pepper strips and cook for 3 minutes until softened. Pour in diced tomatoes, oregano, and thyme. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
  4. Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up, nestling them into the sauce. Scatter olives around the chicken. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 14–16 minutes until chicken is cooked through and an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) is reached.
  5. Remove the lid, increase heat to medium, and cook for 2 more minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce slightly. Scatter fresh parsley over the top before serving.
FODMAP Tip: Always check canned tomato labels — many brands add garlic or onion for flavoring. Look for plain diced tomatoes with only tomatoes, tomato juice, and citric acid listed. Whole peeled tomatoes you crush yourself are a reliable alternative. Olives add a briny, satisfying depth here with zero FODMAP concerns.

"Everything Safe" Meatballs in Marinara

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 490 cal GF 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 500g lean ground beef (90% lean)
  • ¼ cup gluten-free breadcrumbs
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused olive oil, divided
  • 2 tablespoons fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
  • ½ teaspoon dried oregano
  • ½ teaspoon fine sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, plain (no garlic or onion added)
  • 1 teaspoon dried basil
  • Fresh basil leaves to serve

Instructions

  1. In a large bowl, combine ground beef, GF breadcrumbs, egg, 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper. Mix with your hands until just combined — do not overwork or the meatballs will be dense. Form into 16 equal balls (about 2 tablespoons each).
  2. Heat the remaining tablespoon of garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches if needed, brown the meatballs for 3–4 minutes, turning every minute or so, until all sides are deep golden brown. The meatballs do not need to be cooked through at this stage.
  3. Pour crushed tomatoes into the skillet around the meatballs. Add dried basil and stir gently to combine. Bring the sauce to a simmer.
  4. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 12–14 minutes until meatballs are cooked through (internal temperature 160°F / 71°C) and the sauce has thickened. Shake the pan gently every few minutes rather than stirring, to keep meatballs intact.
  5. Serve over GF spaghetti or polenta, topped with fresh basil leaves.
FODMAP Tip: The biggest hidden trap in store-bought meatballs and marinara is onion and garlic — they are in nearly every brand. Making both from scratch in under 30 minutes is genuinely the safer and more economical option. Double the batch and freeze uncooked meatballs on a baking sheet before transferring to a zip-lock bag — they keep for up to 3 months.

Sixty recipes in, and here's what I want you to remember: this food is not a consolation prize. These are real meals that taste like the food you've always loved, made safe for your gut. The family won't know the difference. That's the whole point.

Next up: the vegetarian and vegan chapter, where we tackle the surprisingly solvable problem of hitting your protein goals without beans, garlic, or compromise.

Chapter 8: The Vegetarian & Vegan Macro Niche

Anya had been vegetarian for three years before her IBS diagnosis. Her doctor's printout told her to avoid garlic, onion, most beans, lentils, and wheat. She stared at that list and thought: what's left? I get it. I really do.

Hitting Protein Goals Without High-FODMAP Beans

Here's the myth I hear constantly: you can't eat high-protein, plant-based, and low FODMAP at the same time. That's simply not true — it just requires knowing which proteins are actually safe.

Firm tofu and tempeh are your best friends here. Both are low FODMAP in standard servings (150 g firm tofu, 75 g tempeh per sitting). The key is firm or extra-firm tofu — the pressing process removes the water-soluble FODMAPs that silken tofu retains. Tempeh goes through fermentation, which also reduces fermentable carbohydrates significantly.

Edamame is another power move — but only up to ½ cup shelled (or about 90 g). Go beyond that and you'll stack up GOS. Same rule applies to canned, rinsed lentils and chickpeas: ¼ cup (about 46 g) per serving keeps you solidly in the green zone. Rinse them aggressively — 60 seconds under cold running water — to flush out the fermentable liquid that accumulates in the can.

Quinoa, walnuts, pecans, and sunflower seeds round out the protein toolkit. Quinoa delivers about 8 g of protein per cooked cup. Walnuts bring 4 g per ounce plus omega-3s. Nutritional yeast adds a cheesy, savory punch and packs about 5 g of protein per 2 tablespoons.

Every recipe in this chapter targets 350–600 calories with adequate protein noted. I've also flagged the specific FODMAP threshold for any borderline ingredient, so you know exactly where your limit sits. No guessing. No stacking accidents.

61. Firm Tofu Stir-Fry with Sesame & Ginger

⏱ 20 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 390 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 300 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed (1-inch pieces)
  • 2 tablespoons tamari (gluten-free soy sauce)
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon freshly grated ginger
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon sesame seeds
  • 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced thin
  • 1 cup bok choy, roughly chopped
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • 1 cup cooked white rice (for serving)
  • ¼ teaspoon red chili flakes (optional)

Instructions

  1. Press tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes. Pat dry and cut into 1-inch cubes.
  2. Whisk together tamari, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and grated ginger in a small bowl. Set aside.
  3. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high heat for 1 minute.
  4. Add tofu cubes in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until golden on the bottom. Flip and cook another 3 minutes.
  5. Push tofu to one side. Add red bell pepper and bok choy to the empty side. Stir-fry 2–3 minutes until softened but still crisp.
  6. Pour sauce over everything and toss to coat. Cook 1 minute more until sauce coats all pieces.
  7. Remove from heat. Top with sesame seeds, green onion tops, and chili flakes if using.
  8. Serve immediately over ½ cup cooked white rice per person.
FODMAP Tip: Use only the green tops of spring onions — the white bulb contains fructans. Garlic-infused oil delivers garlic flavor without the fructans that leach into water-based cooking.

62. Hearty Tempeh "Bacon" BLT (GF Bread)

⏱ 25 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 430 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 150 g tempeh, sliced into thin strips (about 3 mm thick)
  • 2 tablespoons tamari
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • 4 slices gluten-free sourdough bread
  • 2 tablespoons vegan mayonnaise (check label for no garlic/onion)
  • 4 large leaves romaine lettuce
  • 1 medium tomato, sliced (up to 2 medium slices per serving)
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions

  1. Whisk together tamari, maple syrup, smoked paprika, and cumin in a shallow dish.
  2. Add tempeh strips to the marinade and turn to coat. Let sit 10 minutes at room temperature.
  3. Heat garlic-infused oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add tempeh strips in a single layer.
  4. Cook 2–3 minutes per side until strips are caramelized and slightly crispy on the edges. Remove and drain on paper towels.
  5. Toast GF bread slices until golden, about 2 minutes in toaster or under broiler.
  6. Spread 1 tablespoon vegan mayonnaise on each of 2 bread slices. Season tomato slices with ¼ teaspoon sea salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper.
  7. Layer: lettuce, tempeh strips, tomato slices. Close sandwich with second bread slice.
  8. Cut diagonally and serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Tempeh is safe at 75 g per serving — this recipe uses 75 g per person. Always check vegan mayo labels; some contain garlic or onion powder as hidden triggers.

63. The Vegan "No-Cheese" Quesadilla

⏱ 20 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 420 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 small corn tortillas (certified GF)
  • 150 g firm tofu, crumbled
  • 3 tablespoons nutritional yeast
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • ½ teaspoon turmeric powder
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ medium red bell pepper, diced fine
  • ½ cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed well (max ¼ cup per serving)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil (for pan)

Instructions

  1. In a bowl, mix crumbled tofu with nutritional yeast, turmeric, smoked paprika, and sea salt until evenly combined.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add diced red pepper and cook 2–3 minutes until softened.
  3. Add tofu mixture to the skillet. Stir and cook 3–4 minutes until heated through and slightly golden.
  4. Stir in rinsed black beans and cilantro. Cook 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
  5. Wipe skillet clean and heat olive oil over medium heat. Place one corn tortilla flat.
  6. Spoon half the tofu-bean filling onto one side of the tortilla. Fold over. Press gently with spatula.
  7. Cook 2 minutes per side until tortilla is golden and crisp. Repeat for second quesadilla.
  8. Cut each into wedges and serve with a side of plain lactose-free yogurt if desired.
FODMAP Tip: Black beans are high FODMAP in large amounts. Keep each serving to ¼ cup (about 46 g) rinsed canned — the rinsing removes roughly 40% of the fermentable carbohydrates.

64. Roasted Eggplant & Quinoa Bowl

⏱ 35 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 460 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 1 medium eggplant (about 300 g), cubed (2-inch pieces)
  • 1 cup dry quinoa, rinsed
  • 2 cups low-sodium vegetable broth (no onion/garlic)
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved (max ½ cup per serving)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons tahini (sesame paste)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Toss eggplant cubes with garlic-infused oil, cumin, smoked paprika, sea salt, and black pepper. Spread in a single layer on baking sheet.
  3. Roast 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until eggplant is golden brown and tender.
  4. While eggplant roasts, combine rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat.
  5. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until broth is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
  6. In a small bowl, whisk tahini with 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 2 tablespoons water until smooth and pourable.
  7. Divide quinoa between two bowls. Top with roasted eggplant and cherry tomatoes.
  8. Drizzle with tahini dressing and garnish with fresh parsley.
FODMAP Tip: Eggplant is low FODMAP in servings up to 75 g. Keep to one medium eggplant shared between two people. Tahini (sesame paste) is safe in 2-tablespoon servings.

65. Peanut Butter Tofu Noodles

⏱ 20 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 520 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 200 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed
  • 150 g rice noodles (flat, medium width)
  • 3 tablespoons natural peanut butter (no added sugar or additives)
  • 2 tablespoons tamari
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 medium carrot, julienned
  • 1 cup baby spinach
  • 3 tablespoons warm water
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • 1 teaspoon sesame seeds

Instructions

  1. Cook rice noodles according to package directions (usually 6–8 minutes in boiling water). Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
  2. Whisk together peanut butter, tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, and warm water until smooth. Adjust consistency with more water if needed — it should pour off a spoon.
  3. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes and cook 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
  4. Add julienned carrot and cook 2 minutes. Add baby spinach and toss until just wilted, about 1 minute.
  5. Add drained noodles to the skillet. Pour peanut sauce over everything and toss to coat evenly over medium heat for 1–2 minutes.
  6. Divide into bowls. Top with green onion tops and sesame seeds.
FODMAP Tip: Natural peanut butter is low FODMAP at 2 tablespoons per serving. Avoid brands with added honey or high-fructose corn syrup. Rice noodles are always a safe, wheat-free base.

66. Edamame & Brown Rice Power Bowl

⏱ 25 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 490 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 cup dry brown rice
  • 2 cups water
  • 1 cup shelled frozen edamame (about 155 g)
  • 1 medium cucumber, diced
  • 1 medium carrot, grated
  • 2 tablespoons tamari
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1 tablespoon sesame seeds
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • ½ teaspoon red chili flakes (optional)

Instructions

  1. Combine brown rice and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 20 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff.
  2. Cook edamame according to package directions (usually 3–5 minutes in boiling salted water). Drain and set aside.
  3. Whisk together tamari, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and grated ginger in a small bowl to make the dressing.
  4. Divide cooked rice between two bowls.
  5. Top each bowl with ½ cup edamame, diced cucumber, and grated carrot.
  6. Drizzle dressing over each bowl. Garnish with sesame seeds, green onion tops, and chili flakes if using.
FODMAP Tip: Edamame is safe at up to ½ cup (90 g) shelled per serving. This recipe uses ½ cup per person, which is right at the threshold — don't add more as a snack the same day.

67. The "Safe" Lentil Stew (Canned/Rinsed Only)

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 340 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 cans (400 g each) canned green lentils, drained and rinsed under cold water for 60 seconds
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 medium carrot, diced
  • 2 stalks celery (leaves removed), sliced thin
  • 1 can (400 g) diced tomatoes (no garlic/onion added)
  • 2 cups low-sodium vegetable broth (no onion/garlic)
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • ½ teaspoon turmeric
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add carrot and celery. Cook 4–5 minutes until softened.
  2. Add cumin, turmeric, smoked paprika, sea salt, and black pepper. Stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Add diced tomatoes (with juice), vegetable broth, and rinsed lentils. Stir to combine.
  4. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  5. Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice and fresh parsley.
  6. Serve immediately or allow to cool and store in airtight containers up to 4 days in the refrigerator.
FODMAP Tip: Canned lentils are lower FODMAP than dried because the fermentable carbohydrates leach into the canning liquid. Always drain AND rinse. Serving size here is ¼ cup lentils — spread across 4 portions the stew stays safely in the green zone.

68. Vegan Creamy Tomato Pasta (Cashew-Free)

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 450 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 350 g gluten-free pasta (rice-based or corn-based)
  • 1 can (400 g) crushed tomatoes (no garlic/onion)
  • ½ cup canned coconut cream (full fat, first-press)
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • ½ teaspoon dried basil
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • ¼ teaspoon red chili flakes
  • 3 tablespoons nutritional yeast
  • ½ cup baby spinach, packed
  • 1 tablespoon fresh basil (for garnish)

Instructions

  1. Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve ¼ cup pasta water before draining.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add oregano and basil; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Add crushed tomatoes, coconut cream, sea salt, black pepper, and chili flakes. Stir to combine.
  4. Simmer over medium-low heat 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
  5. Stir in nutritional yeast. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
  6. Add baby spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
  7. Add drained pasta and toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water 1 tablespoon at a time.
  8. Serve immediately with fresh basil on top.
FODMAP Tip: Canned coconut cream is low FODMAP up to ½ cup per serving. Many vegan creamy pasta sauces use cashews — skip them here. Cashews are high FODMAP at typical serving sizes.

69. Zesty Tofu Scramble

⏱ 15 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 360 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 300 g firm tofu, pressed and crumbled into rough chunks
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • ½ teaspoon turmeric
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ medium red bell pepper, diced
  • 1 cup baby spinach
  • 3 tablespoons nutritional yeast
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • 2 slices gluten-free toast (for serving)

Instructions

  1. Press tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes to remove excess moisture. Crumble into rough, irregular chunks — not too fine.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
  3. Add red bell pepper. Cook 2–3 minutes until softened.
  4. Add crumbled tofu. Sprinkle with turmeric, smoked paprika, sea salt, and black pepper. Stir to coat evenly.
  5. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tofu has a light golden color.
  6. Add baby spinach and nutritional yeast. Toss until spinach wilts, about 1 minute.
  7. Remove from heat. Squeeze lemon juice over the scramble and top with green onion tops.
  8. Serve over toasted GF bread.
FODMAP Tip: Turmeric gives tofu that convincing eggy-yellow color. Nutritional yeast adds a savory, umami depth that makes this feel more substantial. If you want extra protein, serve with a side of lactose-free yogurt.

70. Walnut & Pecan Meatless Tacos

⏱ 20 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 480 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • ¾ cup raw walnuts
  • ¼ cup raw pecans
  • 1 tablespoon tamari
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon chili powder
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • 6 small corn tortillas
  • 1 cup shredded red cabbage
  • ½ medium avocado, sliced (1/8 avocado per taco = low FODMAP)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt

Instructions

  1. Pulse walnuts and pecans in a food processor 8–10 times until roughly chopped — like coarse ground meat texture. Do not over-process into powder.
  2. Heat garlic-infused oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add nut mixture and cook 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently.
  3. Add tamari, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili powder. Stir to coat. Cook 2 more minutes until fragrant and slightly toasted. Season with sea salt.
  4. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side, or wrap in damp paper towels and microwave 30 seconds.
  5. Fill each tortilla with nut meat, shredded cabbage, and avocado slices.
  6. Top with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice.
FODMAP Tip: Walnuts are safe at 10 walnut halves (30 g). Pecans are safe at 10 pecan halves (about 20 g). Avocado is only low FODMAP at 1/8 of a medium fruit — stick to one slice per taco.

71. Crispy Baked Falafel (Chickpea Limits Respected)

⏱ 40 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 310 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 1 can (400 g) canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed thoroughly under cold water for 90 seconds
  • ¼ cup fresh parsley leaves, packed
  • ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, packed
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • ½ teaspoon ground coriander
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 3 tablespoons rice flour (or chickpea flour — just 1 tablespoon)
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil (for brushing)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Pat rinsed chickpeas dry with paper towels — removing moisture is critical for crispiness.
  3. In a food processor, combine chickpeas, parsley, cilantro, garlic-infused oil, cumin, coriander, sea salt, black pepper, and lemon juice. Pulse 12–15 times until mixture resembles coarse crumbs — not a smooth paste.
  4. Transfer to a bowl. Stir in rice flour until mixture holds together when pressed.
  5. Scoop tablespoon-sized portions and shape into flat round patties about 1-inch thick. You should get about 16 pieces.
  6. Place on prepared baking sheet. Brush tops lightly with olive oil.
  7. Bake 25–28 minutes, flipping at 15 minutes, until golden and crispy on both sides.
  8. Serve with tahini drizzle and cucumber slices. Limit to 4 falafel per serving to stay within ¼ cup chickpea threshold.
FODMAP Tip: Canned, rinsed chickpeas are low FODMAP at ¼ cup (46 g) per serving. This recipe divides one 400 g can across 4 servings — each portion lands safely within Monash University guidelines.

72. Sweet Potato & Kale Hash

⏱ 30 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 380 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 medium sweet potato (about 200 g), peeled and diced into ½-inch cubes
