  • 2 cups kale leaves, ribs removed and roughly chopped
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 medium red bell pepper, diced
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
  2. Add sweet potato cubes. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring every 2–3 minutes, until golden on the outside and tender when pierced with a fork.
  3. Add red bell pepper. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
  4. Add smoked paprika, cumin, sea salt, and black pepper. Stir to coat all vegetables.
  5. Add kale and stir. Cook 2–3 minutes until kale wilts but retains a slight bite.
  6. Remove from heat. Top with pumpkin seeds and green onion tops. Drizzle with lemon juice.
FODMAP Tip: Sweet potato is low FODMAP at ½ cup (70 g) diced per serving. This recipe uses about 100 g per person — safely within range. Kale is a low FODMAP green with no serving restrictions from current Monash data.

73. Vegan Coconut Curry with Bamboo Shoots

⏱ 30 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 430 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 300 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed
  • 1 can (400 ml) full-fat coconut milk
  • 1 can (225 g) bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 2 tablespoons red curry paste (check label: no garlic/onion — or make your own with ginger, lemongrass, red chili, lime zest)
  • 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
  • 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced
  • 1 cup baby bok choy, halved
  • 1 tablespoon tamari
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • 2 cups cooked jasmine rice (for serving)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions

  1. Heat garlic-infused oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add curry paste and turmeric. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant and oil has turned a deep orange-red.
  2. Add tofu cubes and cook 3–4 minutes, turning once, until lightly coated in the paste.
  3. Pour in coconut milk and tamari. Stir to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.
  4. Add bamboo shoots and red bell pepper. Simmer 8–10 minutes over medium-low heat.
  5. Add baby bok choy in the final 3 minutes — it should be just tender but not mushy.
  6. Remove from heat and add lime juice. Taste and adjust tamari if needed.
  7. Serve over ½ cup jasmine rice per person, topped with fresh cilantro.
FODMAP Tip: Read your curry paste label carefully — most commercial brands contain garlic and onion. If you can't find a safe one, make a quick paste by blending 1 inch fresh ginger, 1 stalk lemongrass (inner part), ½ red chili, and 1 teaspoon lime zest.

74. Miso-Glazed Eggplant Wedges

⏱ 30 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 290 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 medium eggplant (about 300 g), sliced into 8 wedges lengthwise
  • 2 tablespoons white miso paste
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon tamari
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1 tablespoon sesame seeds
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
  2. Whisk together white miso, maple syrup, tamari, garlic-infused oil, sesame oil, ginger, and rice vinegar in a small bowl until smooth.
  3. Score eggplant wedges in a cross-hatch pattern on the cut side — about ½ inch deep. This helps the glaze penetrate.
  4. Brush glaze generously over the cut sides of all wedges. Place cut-side up on baking sheet.
  5. Roast 20–22 minutes until eggplant is tender and glaze is caramelized and slightly charred at the edges.
  6. Remove from oven. Top with sesame seeds and green onion tops.
FODMAP Tip: White miso is low FODMAP at 2 tablespoons per serving. Red miso has been tested as higher FODMAP — stick to white or shiro miso. This dish pairs well with plain white rice to build a complete meal.

75. The "Cheesy" Nutritional Yeast Popcorn Bowl

⏱ 10 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 280 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • ½ cup popcorn kernels (about 100 g unpopped)
  • 2 tablespoons coconut oil or olive oil
  • 4 tablespoons nutritional yeast
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon turmeric (optional, for deeper color)

Instructions

  1. Heat oil in a large, deep pot with a lid over medium-high heat. Add 3 kernels and cover.
  2. When those 3 kernels pop, add remaining kernels in a single layer and cover tightly.
  3. Shake pot every 10 seconds. Cook until popping slows to 2–3 seconds between pops, about 3–4 minutes total.
  4. Remove from heat. Transfer popcorn immediately to a large bowl.
  5. While still hot, sprinkle nutritional yeast, sea salt, smoked paprika, and turmeric over popcorn. Toss vigorously to coat every kernel.
  6. Serve immediately — popcorn loses crunch within 30 minutes.
FODMAP Tip: Plain popcorn is fully low FODMAP. Nutritional yeast is safe and adds a savory, almost-parmesan flavor. Avoid any store-bought flavored popcorn — most contain onion or garlic powder as the second ingredient.

76. Roasted Root Vegetable Medley

⏱ 40 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 220 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
  • 2 medium parsnips, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
  • 1 medium sweet potato (200 g), peeled and cubed
  • 1 medium turnip, peeled and cubed
  • 3 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment.
  2. In a large bowl, toss all vegetables with garlic-infused oil, rosemary, thyme, sea salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
  3. Spread in a single layer on baking sheet — do not crowd. Use two trays if needed.
  4. Roast 30 minutes, stirring at 15 minutes.
  5. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup and balsamic vinegar. Drizzle over vegetables in the final 5 minutes of roasting for a sticky glaze.
  6. Roast 5 more minutes until edges are caramelized. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Parsnips are low FODMAP up to 75 g per serving. This recipe uses 1 parsnip across 4 servings — each portion contains roughly 50 g. Turnip is low FODMAP with no current serving restriction from Monash data.

77. Vegan "Mac & Cheese" (Potato/Carrot Sauce)

⏱ 35 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 480 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 350 g gluten-free elbow pasta (rice-based)
  • 2 medium Yukon Gold potatoes (about 300 g), peeled and cubed
  • 2 medium carrots, peeled and chopped
  • ¼ cup nutritional yeast
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • ½ cup unsweetened almond milk (or lactose-free milk)
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ teaspoon turmeric
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon white pepper
  • ½ teaspoon Dijon mustard

Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potato and carrot pieces. Boil 12–15 minutes until completely soft when pierced with a fork. Reserve ½ cup of the cooking water.
  2. Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
  3. Transfer cooked potato and carrot to a blender. Add nutritional yeast, garlic-infused oil, almond milk, lemon juice, sea salt, turmeric, smoked paprika, white pepper, and Dijon mustard.
  4. Blend on high for 60 seconds until completely smooth. Add reserved cooking water 2 tablespoons at a time if needed to reach a pourable consistency.
  5. Taste sauce — it should be savory, slightly tangy, and rich. Adjust salt or lemon as needed.
  6. Pour sauce over drained pasta and toss to coat thoroughly. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: This sauce gets its orange "cheesy" color from carrots and turmeric — no artificial dyes needed. Unlike cashew cream alternatives, this sauce is safe for anyone following low FODMAP because both potato and carrot are fully green-light ingredients.

78. Simple Soba Noodles with Tamari

⏱ 15 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 350 cal Vegan | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 200 g 100% buckwheat soba noodles (check label: buckwheat only, no wheat)
  • 3 tablespoons tamari
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1 teaspoon maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • 1 medium cucumber, julienned or spiralized
  • 1 medium carrot, grated
  • 2 tablespoons sesame seeds
  • 3 green spring onion stalks (green tops only), sliced
  • ¼ teaspoon red chili flakes (optional)

Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add soba noodles and cook 4–5 minutes until just tender — do not overcook. Drain and rinse immediately under cold water to stop cooking and remove excess starch.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together tamari, sesame oil, garlic-infused oil, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and maple syrup.
  3. Add drained noodles, cucumber, and grated carrot to the bowl. Toss to coat everything in the dressing.
  4. Divide between two bowls. Top with sesame seeds, green onion tops, and chili flakes if using.
  5. Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 1 day. Add a splash of water and re-toss before serving from cold.
FODMAP Tip: Many soba noodles are a 70/30 blend of buckwheat and wheat — those are not GF. Look for 100% buckwheat soba. Buckwheat is naturally gluten-free and low FODMAP despite the name.

79. Tofu "Chicken" Nuggets

⏱ 35 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 420 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 300 g extra-firm tofu, pressed 15 minutes and torn into nugget-shaped chunks
  • ½ cup rice flour
  • ½ cup gluten-free breadcrumbs
  • ¼ cup unsweetened almond milk
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ teaspoon dried thyme
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
  2. Press tofu firmly for 15 minutes. Tear into uneven nugget shapes — the rough edges create more crunch.
  3. Set up a breading station: bowl 1 with rice flour + smoked paprika + salt + pepper + thyme; bowl 2 with almond milk; bowl 3 with GF breadcrumbs + nutritional yeast.
  4. Working one piece at a time: dredge in rice flour mixture, dip in almond milk, then press into breadcrumb mixture to coat.
  5. Place breaded nuggets on baking sheet. Brush lightly with garlic-infused oil.
  6. Bake 20–22 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crispy on all sides.
  7. Serve with plain mustard or a safe dipping sauce (tamari + maple syrup + rice vinegar).
FODMAP Tip: Check your GF breadcrumb label carefully. Some brands add garlic or onion powder. If you can't find a clean brand, pulse GF sourdough bread in a food processor and toast the crumbs in a dry pan for 3 minutes.

80. The Ultimate Veggie Burger (Quinoa Base)

⏱ 40 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 510 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 1½ cups cooked quinoa (cooled)
  • ½ cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (¼ cup per burger)
  • ¼ cup grated carrot
  • ¼ cup finely chopped red bell pepper
  • 3 tablespoons rice flour
  • 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast
  • 1 tablespoon tamari
  • 1 tablespoon garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed + 5 tablespoons water (flax egg — mix, let sit 5 min)
  • 4 gluten-free burger buns
  • Romaine lettuce, tomato slices, and Dijon mustard for serving

Instructions

  1. Prepare flax egg: combine ground flaxseed and water, stir well, and let sit 5 minutes until gel-like.
  2. In a large bowl, mash rinsed chickpeas roughly with a fork — leave some texture, not a smooth paste.
  3. Add cooked quinoa, grated carrot, red bell pepper, rice flour, nutritional yeast, tamari, garlic-infused oil, smoked paprika, cumin, sea salt, and black pepper. Add flax egg.
  4. Mix until everything holds together when pressed. If mixture is too wet, add 1 more tablespoon rice flour.
  5. Divide into 4 equal portions. Shape into ¾-inch thick patties.
  6. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook patties 4–5 minutes per side until golden-brown crust forms and they hold together when flipped.
  7. Alternatively, bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway.
  8. Serve on toasted GF buns with lettuce, tomato, and mustard.
FODMAP Tip: This burger uses ¼ cup canned, rinsed chickpeas per patty — the safe Monash threshold. Quinoa binds the patty and adds protein. Make a batch on Sunday; patties keep refrigerated up to 3 days or frozen up to 1 month.

Chapter 9: Safe Snacks, Sides, and "Oops I Craved It" Desserts

Anya used to eat a sleeve of crackers over the sink at 10 PM because she'd restricted herself so hard all day she couldn't think straight. Sound familiar? The snack void is real — and it doesn't have to mean punishment food.

Navigating Cravings Without the Punishment

Here's what I figured out the hard way: deprivation feeds cravings. When you white-knuckle it through an entire day on safe but boring meals, your brain is going to scream for sugar and fat by evening. The answer isn't willpower — it's having satisfying, safe options within arm's reach before the craving arrives.

This chapter covers two categories. First, sides that feel indulgent without triggering symptoms — mashed potatoes done right, crispy kale chips, maple-glazed carrots that taste like they belong on a holiday table. Second, the desserts. Real ones. Chocolate brownies, cookies, rice pudding, sorbet. Not "healthy versions" that taste like sawdust and disappointment. Actual desserts that happen to be low FODMAP.

The critical rules for sweets: avoid high-fructose corn syrup (excess fructose stacks immediately), stick to dark chocolate with 70% cacao or higher (lower sugar content), use lactose-free dairy or plant-based milks where needed, and watch your portion on anything with honey or agave — both are high-fructose and need to be completely cut in the elimination phase.

Maple syrup is your sweetener here. It's low FODMAP in tablespoon servings and adds a genuine depth of flavor. White and raw cane sugar are also fine. Keep your individual dessert portions modest — even safe ingredients can stack if you eat half a cake.

81. 3-Ingredient Peanut Butter Cookies

⏱ 20 min 👥 12 cookies 🔥 120 cal each GF | Vegan Option | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 cup natural peanut butter (smooth, no added sugar or oils)
  • ½ cup white granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg (or 1 flax egg for vegan: 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed + 3 tablespoons water)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a bowl, mix peanut butter, sugar, and egg (or flax egg) until a uniform dough forms — it will be thick and slightly oily.
  3. Scoop tablespoon-sized balls and place 2 inches apart on baking sheet.
  4. Press each ball flat with a fork in a cross-hatch pattern to about ½-inch thick.
  5. Bake 10–12 minutes until edges are set and tops are no longer glossy. Do not overbake — cookies firm up as they cool.
  6. Let cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring. They are fragile when warm.
FODMAP Tip: Natural peanut butter (just peanuts and salt) is low FODMAP. Avoid "reduced fat" versions — they often replace fat with corn syrup solids. Limit to 2 cookies per serving to stay within safe peanut butter thresholds.

82. The "No-Bake" Chocolate Energy Bites

⏱ 15 min + 30 min chill 👥 16 bites 🔥 95 cal each Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 cup certified GF rolled oats
  • ½ cup natural peanut butter
  • 3 tablespoons maple syrup
  • 3 tablespoons dark chocolate chips (70% cacao or higher)
  • 2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 1 tablespoon chia seeds
  • ½ teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 tablespoon coconut oil (melted)

Instructions

  1. In a large bowl, combine all ingredients. Mix until a uniform, sticky dough forms that holds together when pressed.
  2. If mixture is too dry, add 1 teaspoon coconut oil at a time. If too sticky, refrigerate 10 minutes before rolling.
  3. Scoop tablespoon-sized portions and roll into tight balls between your palms.
  4. Place on a parchment-lined plate. Refrigerate 30 minutes to firm up.
  5. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator up to 1 week or freeze up to 1 month.
FODMAP Tip: GF rolled oats are low FODMAP at ½ cup (52 g) per serving. Dark chocolate chips (70%+) are safe at 30 g. Avoid chocolate chips with milk solids listed — that's added lactose.

83. Safe Berry Crumble

⏱ 40 min 👥 6 servings 🔥 260 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 2 cups fresh or frozen blueberries
  • 1 cup fresh or frozen strawberries, hulled and halved
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup (for fruit)
  • 1 tablespoon cornstarch
  • 1 teaspoon lemon juice
  • 1 cup certified GF rolled oats
  • ¼ cup rice flour
  • 3 tablespoons maple syrup (for crumble)
  • 3 tablespoons coconut oil (solid)
  • ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a baking dish (8x8 inch), toss blueberries and strawberries with 1 tablespoon maple syrup, cornstarch, and lemon juice. Spread evenly.
  3. In a separate bowl, combine rolled oats, rice flour, 3 tablespoons maple syrup, coconut oil, cinnamon, and sea salt. Use your fingers to rub the coconut oil into the oat mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs with some larger clumps.
  4. Spread crumble topping evenly over the berry layer.
  5. Bake 30–32 minutes until topping is golden brown and berry juices are bubbling around the edges.
  6. Cool 10 minutes before serving. Serve with lactose-free vanilla yogurt or a scoop of dairy-free ice cream.
FODMAP Tip: Blueberries are safe at ¼ cup per serving; strawberries at 5 medium berries. This recipe's portions per serving stay within both thresholds. Avoid raspberries in large amounts — they become moderate FODMAP above ¼ cup.

84. Lactose-Free Vanilla Rice Pudding

⏱ 35 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 280 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • ¾ cup short-grain white rice (Arborio works well)
  • 2 cups lactose-free whole milk
  • 1 cup water
  • 3 tablespoons white sugar
  • 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon (for serving)
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt

Instructions

  1. Combine rice, water, and sea salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
  2. Add lactose-free milk and sugar. Stir well. Increase heat to medium.
  3. Cook uncovered, stirring every 2–3 minutes to prevent sticking, for 18–20 minutes until mixture thickens to a creamy, porridge-like consistency. It will thicken further as it cools.
  4. Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract.
  5. Serve warm or chill. Dust with ground cinnamon before serving.
FODMAP Tip: Lactose-free milk has the lactase enzyme added, breaking down lactose completely. Regular milk will trigger symptoms in lactose-intolerant individuals — even a small amount. This pudding keeps in the fridge for 3 days; stir in 1 tablespoon milk when reheating to restore creaminess.

85. Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies (GF)

⏱ 25 min 👥 18 cookies 🔥 145 cal each GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1¼ cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (rice flour base)
  • ½ teaspoon baking soda
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ cup (115 g) unsalted butter, softened (or coconut oil for vegan)
  • ½ cup white granulated sugar
  • ¼ cup packed light brown sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • ¾ cup dark chocolate chips (70%+ cacao, dairy-free if needed)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
  2. Whisk GF flour, baking soda, and sea salt in a bowl. Set aside.
  3. Beat butter and both sugars in a large bowl with a hand mixer on medium speed, 2 minutes until fluffy and pale.
  4. Beat in egg and vanilla extract, 30 seconds.
  5. Add flour mixture to the butter mixture and stir with a spatula until just combined — do not overmix.
  6. Fold in chocolate chips.
  7. Drop tablespoon-sized portions 2 inches apart on baking sheets.
  8. Bake 11–13 minutes until edges are golden but centers look just barely set.
  9. Cool on baking sheet 5 minutes — they firm up as they cool.
FODMAP Tip: GF flour blends vary — look for ones without added inulin or chicory root, which are high FODMAP. Bob's Red Mill 1-to-1 and King Arthur Measure for Measure are both tested and safe options.

86. Refreshing Cantaloupe Sorbet

⏱ 10 min + 4 hr freeze 👥 4 servings 🔥 90 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 4 cups cantaloupe, peeled and cubed (about ½ medium cantaloupe)
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice
  • 2 tablespoons white sugar
  • ¼ cup water
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt

Instructions

  1. In a small saucepan over low heat, combine sugar and water. Stir until sugar dissolves completely, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and cool.
  2. Blend cantaloupe cubes, lime juice, cooled simple syrup, and sea salt in a blender on high speed for 60 seconds until completely smooth.
  3. Pour into a shallow freezer-safe container. Cover and freeze 2 hours.
  4. Scrape and stir with a fork to break up ice crystals. Return to freezer 2 more hours.
  5. Scrape again vigorously before serving to achieve a scoopable texture.
  6. Alternatively, blend frozen mixture in a food processor for a smoother texture.
FODMAP Tip: Cantaloupe is low FODMAP at 1/2 cup (90 g) per serving — this recipe serves 4, putting each portion at exactly 90 g. Watermelon is a common swap but is very high fructose — keep using cantaloupe here.

87. The "Safe" Dark Chocolate Brownie

⏱ 35 min 👥 16 brownies 🔥 160 cal each GF

Ingredients

  • ½ cup (115 g) unsalted butter
  • 100 g dark chocolate (70%+ cacao), roughly chopped
  • ¾ cup white granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • ½ cup rice flour
  • 2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ teaspoon baking powder

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang on two sides for easy removal.
  2. Melt butter and chopped dark chocolate together in a heatproof bowl over a pot of simmering water (double boiler), stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and cool 5 minutes.
  3. Whisk sugar into the chocolate mixture until combined. Add eggs one at a time, whisking well after each. Add vanilla extract.
  4. Sift rice flour, cocoa powder, sea salt, and baking powder into the chocolate mixture. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined — a few streaks of flour are fine.
  5. Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top.
  6. Bake 22–24 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with moist crumbs (not wet batter).
  7. Cool completely in pan before cutting into 16 squares.
FODMAP Tip: Dark chocolate (70%+) is low FODMAP at 30 g per serving. This recipe uses 100 g across 16 brownies — about 6 g per brownie, well within range. The rice flour keeps these GF and actually produces a fudgier texture than wheat flour.

88. Crispy Roasted Potato Wedges

⏱ 40 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 230 cal Vegan | GF

Ingredients

  • 4 medium russet potatoes (about 800 g total), scrubbed
  • 3 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon dried rosemary
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon cornstarch (the secret to maximum crispiness)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C). Place a baking sheet in the oven while it preheats — a hot pan is critical for crispy wedges.
  2. Cut each potato into 8 wedges lengthwise.
  3. Place wedges in a large bowl. Cover with cold water and soak 10 minutes to remove surface starch. Drain and dry completely with paper towels — this step is essential.
  4. Return dry wedges to the bowl. Toss with garlic-infused oil, smoked paprika, rosemary, sea salt, and black pepper. Sprinkle cornstarch and toss again to coat evenly.
  5. Carefully remove hot baking sheet from oven. Spread wedges cut-side down in a single layer — do not crowd.
  6. Roast 25–30 minutes, flipping at 15 minutes, until deeply golden and crispy on the outside.
  7. Serve immediately with a side of plain mustard or lactose-free sour cream.
FODMAP Tip: Potatoes are fully low FODMAP with no serving restrictions. The cornstarch coat creates a crackly exterior — don't skip it. Garlic-infused oil gives the garlic flavor the whole family craves without the fructans.

89. Garlic-Infused Mashed Potatoes

⏱ 25 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 280 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 900 g Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and quartered
  • 3 tablespoons garlic-infused oil
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter (or vegan butter)
  • ½ cup lactose-free whole milk, warmed
  • ¾ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon white pepper
  • 2 tablespoons fresh chives, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions

  1. Place quartered potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water by 1 inch. Bring to a boil.
  2. Boil 15–18 minutes until potatoes are completely tender and fall apart easily when pierced with a fork.
  3. Drain thoroughly. Return to the warm pot over low heat for 1 minute to steam off excess moisture — this prevents gluey mashed potatoes.
  4. Add butter and garlic-infused oil. Mash with a potato masher or potato ricer to desired smoothness.
  5. Add warm lactose-free milk 2 tablespoons at a time, folding gently. Do not overwork — stop when smooth and creamy.
  6. Season with sea salt and white pepper. Top with fresh chives.
FODMAP Tip: Use a potato ricer for the silkiest texture — it prevents overworking the starch. Never use a food processor or blender for mashed potatoes; overmixing releases starch and creates a paste. Regular butter is low FODMAP because it contains almost no lactose.

90. Simple Buttered Green Beans

⏱ 10 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 90 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 450 g fresh green beans, trimmed
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest

Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans and cook exactly 3–4 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green.
  2. Transfer immediately to a bowl of ice water for 2 minutes to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well.
  3. In a large skillet over medium heat, melt butter. Add drained green beans and toss to coat.
  4. Cook 2 minutes until heated through. Season with sea salt, black pepper, lemon juice, and lemon zest.
  5. Toss once more and serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Green beans are low FODMAP up to ¼ cup (46 g). Keep each serving to about 110 g — that's a generous portion within Monash limits. Do not use canned green beans here; fresh or frozen give far better texture.

91. Homemade Tortilla Chips with Tomato-Free Salsa

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 200 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 8 small corn tortillas, cut into 6 triangles each
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • For the salsa:
  • 1 medium cucumber, finely diced
  • 1 medium red bell pepper, finely diced
  • 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon ground cumin

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
  2. Place tortilla triangles in a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, sea salt, and smoked paprika. Toss to coat evenly.
  3. Spread in a single layer across both baking sheets.
  4. Bake 10–12 minutes, rotating pans halfway, until chips are golden and crisp. Watch closely after 9 minutes — they burn fast.
  5. While chips bake, combine all salsa ingredients in a bowl. Stir well and adjust lime juice and salt to taste.
  6. Cool chips 3 minutes before serving with the salsa alongside.
FODMAP Tip: Traditional salsa uses tomatoes, which are low FODMAP up to ½ cup. However, canned or crushed tomatoes with added garlic/onion are a hidden trigger — this cucumber-pepper salsa eliminates that risk entirely while keeping the crunch factor.

92. Maple-Glazed Carrots

⏱ 20 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 140 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 600 g carrots, peeled and cut diagonally into ½-inch slices
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (or vegan butter)
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup
  • ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves

Instructions

  1. Steam or boil carrot slices 5–6 minutes until just tender — they should still have slight resistance. Drain well.
  2. In a large skillet over medium heat, melt butter. Add maple syrup and cinnamon. Stir 30 seconds.
  3. Add carrots and toss to coat in the glaze. Cook 3–4 minutes, stirring often, until glaze thickens and coats each carrot slice.
  4. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Top with fresh thyme.
  5. Serve immediately — the glaze sets as it cools.
FODMAP Tip: Carrots are fully low FODMAP with no portion restrictions. Maple syrup is safe up to 2 tablespoons per serving — this recipe uses 2 tablespoons across 4 servings, making each portion well within range.

93. Quick Microwave Mug Cake (Chocolate)

⏱ 5 min 👥 1 serving 🔥 320 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 3 tablespoons rice flour
  • 2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 2 tablespoons white granulated sugar
  • ¼ teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 pinch sea salt (⅛ teaspoon)
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons lactose-free milk
  • 2 tablespoons coconut oil or melted butter
  • ½ teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • 1 tablespoon dark chocolate chips (70%+ cacao)

Instructions

  1. In a large microwave-safe mug (at least 12 oz capacity), whisk together rice flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking powder, and sea salt.
  2. Add egg, lactose-free milk, coconut oil, and vanilla extract. Whisk vigorously until smooth — no lumps.
  3. Stir in chocolate chips.
  4. Microwave on HIGH for 60–75 seconds. The cake should rise and set — center will look slightly moist but not liquid. Every microwave is different; start at 60 seconds and add 10-second intervals if needed.
  5. Cool 1 minute before eating — the mug will be extremely hot.
FODMAP Tip: This is a 1-minute emergency dessert. If you overbake, it will turn rubbery — err on the side of slightly underdone. The residual heat finishes the cooking. Almond flour can replace rice flour for a richer texture, but limit to 2 tablespoons almond flour (almonds are moderate-FODMAP above 10 kernels).

94. Plain Rice Crackers with Cheddar Slices

⏱ 5 min 👥 1 serving 🔥 210 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 10 plain rice crackers (check label: rice and salt only)
  • 30 g aged cheddar cheese, sliced thin (about 3 slices)
  • 1 tablespoon natural peanut butter (optional addition)
  • 5 thin slices cucumber

Instructions

  1. Arrange rice crackers on a plate.
  2. Top each cracker with a thin slice of aged cheddar or a spread of peanut butter.
  3. Add a cucumber slice on top of each for freshness and crunch.
  4. Serve immediately.
FODMAP Tip: Aged hard cheeses (cheddar, parmesan, Swiss) are very low in lactose because the aging process breaks it down. Fresh cheeses like ricotta or cream cheese are much higher in lactose. This snack comes together in under 2 minutes and travels well to work.

95. Zesty Lemon Polenta Cake

⏱ 50 min 👥 10 slices 🔥 240 cal per slice GF

Ingredients

  • 1 cup fine polenta (cornmeal)
  • 1 cup almond flour (blanched, finely ground)
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¾ cup white granulated sugar
  • ½ cup (115 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3 large eggs
  • Zest of 2 large lemons (about 2 tablespoons)
  • 3 tablespoons lemon juice
  • ½ teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • 2 tablespoons powdered sugar (for dusting, optional)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C). Grease a 9-inch round cake pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
  2. In a bowl, whisk polenta, almond flour, baking powder, and sea salt. Set aside.
  3. Beat butter and sugar in a large bowl with a hand mixer on medium speed, 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
  4. Beat in eggs one at a time, scraping down the bowl after each addition. Add lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract.
  5. Fold in the dry ingredients until just combined — the batter will be thick.
  6. Spread into prepared pan. Smooth the top with a spatula.
  7. Bake 35–38 minutes until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. The edges should pull slightly from the pan.
  8. Cool 10 minutes in pan, then turn onto a wire rack. Dust with powdered sugar when cool.
FODMAP Tip: Almond flour is safe up to ¼ cup (24 g) per serving. This recipe uses 1 cup across 10 slices — about 24 g per serving, right at the threshold. Don't double the almond flour. The polenta gives this cake a golden, grainy texture that's genuinely satisfying.

96. Crispy Baked Kale Chips

⏱ 20 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 110 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 1 large bunch curly kale (about 200 g), ribs removed, torn into 3-inch pieces
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast (optional, for cheesy flavor)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C). Line two large baking sheets with parchment.
  2. Wash kale thoroughly and dry completely with a salad spinner and paper towels — any moisture will steam the chips instead of crisping them.
  3. In a large bowl, toss kale pieces with olive oil, sea salt, and smoked paprika. If using nutritional yeast, add it now and toss again. Massage oil into every piece.
  4. Spread in a single layer on baking sheets — pieces should not overlap at all.
  5. Bake 18–22 minutes until chips are completely crisp and dry. Check at 15 minutes — edges burn before centers are done.
  6. Cool 2 minutes on pan — they crisp further as they cool. Eat same day.
FODMAP Tip: Kale is free from FODMAPs at all tested serving sizes. The low oven temperature (300°F vs. 400°F) is intentional — low and slow prevents burning while allowing moisture to evaporate fully. Store any leftovers in an open container, not sealed, or they soften overnight.

97. The "Safe" Trail Mix (Macadamia, Pecans, Dark Choc)

⏱ 5 min 👥 6 servings 🔥 220 cal per serving Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • ½ cup macadamia nuts (about 60 g)
  • ½ cup pecan halves (about 60 g)
  • ½ cup pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
  • ¼ cup dark chocolate chips (70%+ cacao, dairy-free)
  • ¼ cup dried cranberries (ensure no added apple juice — just cranberries and sugar)
  • ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt

Instructions

  1. Combine all ingredients in a bowl and toss to distribute evenly.
  2. Divide into 6 equal portions (about ¼ cup each) and store in individual snack bags or small containers.
  3. Store in a cool, dry place up to 2 weeks.
FODMAP Tip: Macadamias are fully low FODMAP (no portion limit from current Monash data). Pecans are safe at 10 halves. Cashews and pistachios are high FODMAP — do not substitute them here. Check dried cranberry labels: some are processed with apple juice concentrate, which adds excess fructose.

98. Strawberry & Kiwi Fruit Salad

⏱ 10 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 90 cal Vegan | GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 cups fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced (about 300 g)
  • 4 medium kiwi fruits, peeled and sliced into rounds
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • ¼ teaspoon lime zest
  • 2 tablespoons fresh mint leaves, torn

Instructions

  1. In a small bowl, whisk maple syrup, lime juice, and lime zest together.
  2. Combine strawberries and kiwi in a large bowl. Pour dressing over the fruit.
  3. Toss gently to coat. Scatter fresh mint on top.
  4. Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 hours — the strawberries will release juice and create a light syrup, which is delicious.
FODMAP Tip: Strawberries are safe at 5 medium berries (65 g) per serving. Kiwi is safe at 2 per serving. This recipe stays within both limits. Avoid adding any other fruits not checked against Monash data — some popular salad additions like mango or apple are high FODMAP.

99. Lactose-Free Cheese Board Guide

⏱ 10 min 👥 4 servings 🔥 320 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • Safe cheeses (choose 2–3):
  • 60 g aged cheddar (12+ months), sliced
  • 60 g Swiss/Gruyère, sliced thin
  • 60 g Parmesan, shaved
  • 60 g Brie (small amount — about 40 g per person, tested low FODMAP)
  • Safe accompaniments:
  • 20 plain rice crackers (check label: rice and salt only)
  • ¼ cup red grapes (about 10 grapes per person)
  • 4 medium strawberries
  • 1 tablespoon walnuts
  • 1 tablespoon pecans
  • 1 tablespoon seedless blueberries
  • 1 tablespoon pure maple syrup (drizzle on Brie if using)

Instructions

  1. Arrange cheeses on a wooden board in separate sections. Slice hard cheeses thin for easier serving.
  2. Place rice crackers in clusters around the cheese.
  3. Fill small bowls or corners of the board with grapes, strawberries, blueberries, walnuts, and pecans.
  4. Drizzle maple syrup over Brie just before serving.
  5. Serve at room temperature — take cheese from refrigerator 20 minutes before serving for best flavor.
FODMAP Tip: Avoid fresh cheeses: ricotta (more than 2 tablespoons), cream cheese (more than 2 tablespoons), and mascarpone are all higher in lactose. Hard, aged cheeses are safe because aging breaks lactose down. Cottage cheese is moderate FODMAP — skip it here. This board doubles as a social entertaining option that no one will know is "restricted."

100. Soothing Peppermint Hot Cocoa

⏱ 8 min 👥 2 servings 🔥 180 cal GF | 30-Min

Ingredients

  • 2 cups lactose-free whole milk (or unsweetened oat milk — max ½ cup oat milk)
  • 3 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 2 tablespoons white granulated sugar
  • ¼ teaspoon pure peppermint extract (not peppermint oil — very potent)
  • ¼ teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  • 1 pinch sea salt (⅛ teaspoon)
  • 1 tablespoon dark chocolate chips (70%+ cacao) for garnish

Instructions

  1. In a small saucepan, whisk together cocoa powder, sugar, and sea salt.
  2. Add 2 tablespoons of the milk and whisk to form a smooth paste — this prevents lumpy cocoa.
  3. Add remaining milk. Heat over medium heat, whisking constantly, until just steaming — do not boil.
  4. Remove from heat. Stir in peppermint extract and vanilla extract. Start with ¼ teaspoon peppermint and add more only after tasting — it's powerful.
  5. Pour into mugs. Float a few dark chocolate chips on top.
FODMAP Tip: Peppermint has been studied for IBS symptom relief — it's one of the few flavors that may actually support gut comfort rather than just being neutral. Avoid peppermint syrup-based cocoa mixes (most contain high-fructose corn syrup). Lactose-free milk makes this completely safe; if using oat milk, cap at ½ cup per serving.

Chapter 10: The 28-Day App-to-Plate Meal Plan

I used to spend Sunday night staring at a blank notebook trying to "meal plan" and ending up with the same three rotating dinners. This plan solves that. Every day, every meal — already decided for you.

This plan runs four weeks. Each week has a clear focus so it doesn't feel like 28 identical days of deprivation. You're building new habits progressively — week one resets your baseline, week four prepares your gut for reintroduction.

Every recipe referenced is numbered from this book. All 100 recipes are used across the plan, which means your shopping list stays tight and repetitive — that's intentional. Familiarity with a recipe cuts your cook time by 40% the second time you make it.

Before You Start: Cook a batch of plain white rice, quinoa, and one protein source every Sunday. These become the backbone of your weekday lunches and take meal prep from 45 minutes to 10.
